mainTopic: When a בית דין is liable for a mistaken ruling: partial versus full cancellation, unfit judges, mistaken versus on-purpose actions, and how many קרבנות are brought.
overview: A בית דין brings a קרבן for a mistaken ruling only when it cancels part of a מצוה and keeps part (ביטול מקצת וקיום מקצת), not when it uproots the whole מצוה (עקירת גוף). רב יוסף asks which of these applies to a ruling that permits all plowing on שבת. Three proofs from the משנה (שומרת יום כנגד יום, הוצאה, השתחויה) are each pushed away, so his question stays unresolved. רבי זירא asks about a ruling of 'no שבת in שביעית', and רבינא proves from a ברייתא about a false נביא that a time-limited cancellation counts as partial. A new משנה exempts the court if one judge objected, if the מופלא was absent, or if any judge was unfit, learned from the word 'עדה'. The גמרא gives the sources for these rules, ending with 'ונשאו אתך'. Another משנה sorts the cases by whether the court and the people acted by mistake or on purpose. An attempt to use it to answer רמי בר חמא's question is turned down. The amud ends with רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagreeing over whether one set of קרבנות is brought or one for each tribe.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks about a ruling that plowing is permitted on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks whether a ruling that permits plowing on שבת counts as partial cancellation or as uprooting the essence of the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked: If the court ruled 'There is no prohibition of plowing on שבת,' what is the law? Do we say that since they agree to everything else about שבת, it is like cancelling part and keeping part? Or perhaps, since they uproot plowing completely, it is like uprooting the essence of the מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks how to classify a court ruling that wipes out one entire מלאכה (plowing) while keeping the rest of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says the court still keeps most of שבת, so this is only partial cancellation, and the court would be liable. The other side says plowing is a complete category of its own, and wiping it out fully looks like uprooting a whole thing, so the court would be exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question with no ready answer)
Plowing, one of the main מלאכות of שבת
Cancelling part of a מצוה and keeping part; the court is liable for this
Uprooting the essence of a מצוה; the court is exempt for this
Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)

steps.whyThisMatters: The question sets up the test for the rest of the sugya: is the measure the whole מצוה or the specific category being wiped out?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked:
If the court ruled 'there is no prohibition of plowing on Shabbat', what is the law?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether the court must bring a קרבן for this mistaken ruling.

phrases.english: Do we say:
since they agree about all the rest of the matter,
it is like cancelling part and keeping part,
or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּקָא עָקְרִיִין לֵיהּ לַחֲרִישָׁהּ כׇּל עִיקָּר,
phrases.english: since they uproot plowing completely,
it is like uprooting the essence of the מצוה?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does wiping out one whole מלאכה count as ביטול מקצת וקיום מקצת or as עקירת גוף?

steps.title: Attempted proof from the case of a woman who watches a day for a day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer from the משנה: the court is liable for ruling that שומרת יום כנגד יום is permitted, even though that seems to uproot a whole category.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'There is a prohibition of נדה in the Torah, but one who has relations with a woman who watches a day for a day is exempt.' And why is the court liable here? Didn't they uproot the law of a woman who watches a day for a day completely?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה's example of a liable court ruling to try to answer רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling seems to wipe out the entire law of שומרת יום כנגד יום, yet the משנה treats it as partial cancellation, and the court is liable. If that is right, wiping out all of plowing should also count as partial cancellation.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her menstrual period, with whom relations are forbidden
A woman who must watch one clean day for each day of discharge

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'There is a prohibition of a menstruating woman in the Torah,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַבָּא עַל שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: 'but one who has relations with a woman who watches a day for a day is exempt.'
phrases.notes: This is the mistaken ruling quoted in the משנה, and the משנה says the court is liable for it.

phrases.english: And why should the court be liable?

phrases.aramaic: הָא עָקְרִיִין לְשׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם כׇּל עִיקָּר!
phrases.english: Didn't they uproot the law of a woman who watches a day for a day completely!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question from step 1
steps.raayaObject: That wiping out one whole category counts as partial cancellation
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's example of the ruling about שומרת יום כנגד יום

steps.title: רב יוסף: that case was already explained differently
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away: the ruling about שומרת יום is to be understood as the גמרא explained earlier, and it was not a full uprooting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף can say to you: The case of the woman who watches a day for a day that they mention is as we explained it earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers on רב יוסף's behalf that the proof does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא explained this ruling as permitting only a narrower point, the first stage of relations, and not the whole law of שומרת יום. Since the law was not fully wiped out, the case tells us nothing about wiping out all of plowing.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)
As we answered or explained earlier

phrases.english: Rav Yosef can say to you:
The woman who watches a day that they mention is as we explained.
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier answer, where the ruling only allowed the first stage of relations and not the whole law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from שומרת יום only
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling in that case was not a full uprooting; it was already explained as covering a narrower point.

steps.title: Second attempted proof from carrying out on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again from the משנה: the court is liable for ruling that carrying from a private to a public domain is permitted, even though that wipes out the whole מלאכה of הוצאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'There is שבת in the Torah, but one who carries out from a private domain to a public domain is exempt.' And why is the court liable here? Didn't they uproot carrying out completely?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second example from the משנה to try to answer רב יוסף. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case matches רב יוסף's question very closely: it involves one entire מלאכה of שבת, הוצאה, being permitted. Since the משנה says the court is liable, it seems that wiping out a whole מלאכה counts as partial cancellation.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries out an object
The מלאכה of carrying between domains

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'There is Shabbat in the Torah,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַמּוֹצִיא מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: 'but one who carries out from a private domain to a public domain is exempt.'
And why should the court be liable?
Didn't they uproot carrying out completely!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא offers a new and closer proof
steps.raayaObject: That wiping out a whole מלאכה of שבת counts as partial cancellation
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's example of the ruling permitting הוצאה

steps.title: The carrying case is also only a partial cancellation
steps.stepSummary: The proof from הוצאה is pushed away. The court only cancelled part of the מלאכה, as explained earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is as we explained.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 4. The ruling about carrying did not wipe out all of הוצאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 claimed that permitting carrying cancels the whole מלאכה of הוצאה, and yet the court is still liable. The answer is that the case should be read the way it was explained earlier: the court cancelled only one part of הוצאה. So it was not a full uprooting, and it tells us nothing about רב יוסף's question.

keyTerms.meaning: as we answered / as we explained earlier

phrases.english: There too, it is as we explained.
phrases.notes: This refers back to the earlier explanation that the court only cancelled one part of carrying, not all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ruling wiped out all of הוצאה. In fact it only cancelled part of it.

steps.title: A new proof from bowing to an idol
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again from the משנה: the court is liable for ruling that one who bows to an idol is exempt, even though that seems to wipe out the whole law of השתחויה. So wiping out a whole category would count as partial cancellation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'There is idol worship in the Torah, but one who bows is exempt.' Why is the court liable? They uprooted bowing completely!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third attempt to answer רב יוסף's question. It uses another case from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the court is liable if it ruled that bowing to an idol is permitted. But השתחויה is a complete form of עבודה זרה on its own, so permitting it seems to wipe that category out entirely. Since the court is still liable, wiping out a whole category should count as ביטול מקצת וקיום מקצת, which would answer רב יוסף about plowing.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: יֵשׁ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בַּתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Come and hear: 'There is idol worship in the Torah,
but one who bows down is exempt.'

phrases.aramaic: אַמַּאי? וְהָא עָקְרִיִין לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָה כׇּל עִיקָּר!
phrases.english: Why should they be liable? They uprooted bowing completely!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: יֵשׁ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 5 pushed away the הוצאה proof, a new proof is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That wiping out one whole category (bowing) counts as partial cancellation, so the court is liable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's example: 'there is idol worship in the Torah, but one who bows is exempt.'

steps.title: Bowing too is only a partial cancellation
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. The ruling about bowing should also be read as cancelling only part of it, as explained earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: bowing too is as we explained.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the bowing proof the same way it rejected the earlier ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling did not permit all bowing to idols. It only permitted one kind or one aspect of it, as explained earlier. So this is a partial cancellation, and רב יוסף's question still has no answer.
steps.whatToRemember: All three proofs (שומרת יום כנגד יום, הוצאה, השתחויה) are pushed away the same way. Each ruling only cancelled part of the law, so רב יוסף's question stays open.

phrases.english: They say: bowing too is as we explained.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 6.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed bowing was fully permitted. In fact only part of it was permitted.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks about a ruling that there is no שבת in שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks what the law is if a court ruled that there is no שבת during the שביעית year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: if a court ruled 'there is no שבת during שביעית,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens, still on the theme of rulings that cancel a מצוה or part of it. רבי זירא wants to know how to treat this kind of ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such a ruling cancels שבת for one whole year, but שבת still applies in the other years. The question is whether the court is liable for it, which depends on how this kind of cancellation is classified.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
If they ruled 'there is no Shabbat in the Sabbatical Year,' what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֵין שַׁבָּת בַּשְּׁבִיעִית, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs for רב יוסף's question end, a related new question is raised.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a court is liable for ruling that שבת does not apply during שביעית.

steps.title: How could the court make such a mistake?
steps.stepSummary: Before dealing with the question, the גמרא asks what led the judges to such a strange ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what did they err?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא wants to know the basis for the mistake before discussing the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court is only liable for a mistake that has some logic behind it. So the גמרא first needs to show how judges could reach the idea that there is no שבת in שביעית.

phrases.english: In what did they err?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the case behind רבי זירא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reasoning that led the court to its mistaken ruling.

steps.title: The mistake came from misreading 'בחריש ובקציר תשבת'
steps.stepSummary: The judges misread the פסוק to mean that שבת applies only in years when there is plowing. In שביעית there is no plowing, so they concluded there is no שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They erred in this verse: 'In plowing and in harvest you shall rest.' They understood it this way: when there is plowing, there is שבת. When there is no plowing, there is no שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. It shows the misreading of a פסוק that could lead a court to this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links resting on שבת to plowing and harvest. The judges read it as a condition: שבת applies only when plowing is allowed. Since plowing is forbidden in שביעית, they wrongly concluded that שבת does not apply that year.
steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the real law. שבת applies in every year, including שביעית. The גמרא is only explaining how a court could have made this mistake.

phrases.english: In this verse:
'In plowing and in harvest you shall rest.'
At a time when there is plowing, there is Shabbat;
and at a time when there is no plowing, there is no Shabbat.
phrases.notes: 'No plowing' means the שביעית year, when working the land is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The judges misread שמות 34:21 to mean that שבת depends on plowing being allowed, so it would not apply in שביעית.
steps.whyThisMatters: Now that the mistake has a basis in a פסוק, the גמרא can go on to discuss whether a court would be liable for it.

steps.title: Partial cancellation or full uprooting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out רבי זירא's question. Does 'no שבת in שביעית' count as cancelling part of שבת or uprooting it entirely?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say: since people still keep שבת in the other six years of the cycle, this is like cancelling part and keeping part? Or perhaps: since they uproot שבת completely during שביעית, it is like uprooting the whole thing?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know why the judges ruled this way, the גמרא states the real question. Which category does this ruling fall into?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that a בית דין brings a קרבן only for cancelling part of a מצוה, not for uprooting all of it. Each side has a good point. שבת is still kept in six of the seven years, but in שביעית itself it is wiped out completely.

keyTerms.meaning: cancelling part and keeping part of a מצוה
the years of the seven-year שמיטה cycle

phrases.english: Do we say:
since they keep it (שבת)
in the rest of the years of the seven-year cycle,
it is like cancelling part and keeping part,
or perhaps:
since they uproot it in the seventh year,
it is like uprooting the whole thing?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן כֵּיוָן דִּמְקַיְּימִין לַהּ בִּשְׁאָר שְׁנֵי שָׁבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the explanation of the judges' reasoning, the גמרא returns to רבי זירא's actual question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a time-limited cancellation of a מצוה count as partial cancellation, which makes the court liable, or as full uprooting, which makes it exempt?

steps.title: רבינא's proof from the false prophet
steps.stepSummary: רבינא cites a ברייתא about a נביא. In it, 'worship today, cancel tomorrow' counts as partial cancellation. So 'no שבת in שביעית' is also partial.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Come and hear. A נביא who prophesies to uproot something from the Torah is liable. If he prophesies to cancel part and keep part, רבי שמעון says he is exempt. But for עבודה זרה, even if he said 'worship it today and cancel it tomorrow,' he is liable. Learn from this: 'no שבת in שביעית' is like cancelling part and keeping part.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question with a ברייתא about a false נביא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats 'worship an idol today but not tomorrow' as an example of cancelling only part. That is why it needs the special rule that עבודה זרה is liable even then. So a cancellation limited to a certain time counts as partial. 'No שבת only in שביעית' is the same kind of time-limited cancellation.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the proof is about the punishment of a prophet. The proof is only about the category: a time-limited cancellation is called 'partial.'

phrases.english: Ravina said: Come and hear:
a prophet who prophesied
to uproot a matter from the Torah is liable.
To cancel part and keep part,
Rabbi Shimon says: he is exempt.
And with idol worship, even if he said:
'Worship it today, and cancel it tomorrow,' he is liable.
phrases.notes: Here is the key: 'today yes, tomorrow no' is treated as a partial cancellation.

phrases.english: Learn from this: 'there is no שבת in the seventh year'
is like cancelling part and keeping part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That 'no שבת in שביעית' counts as partial cancellation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a false נביא. It calls 'worship today, cancel tomorrow' a partial cancellation.

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: 'no שבת in שביעית' counts as partial cancellation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבינא's proof and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ruling counts as partial cancellation, a בית דין that ruled 'no שבת in שביעית' would be liable to bring a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: the bull offering a court brings for a mistaken ruling

steps.whatToRemember: Cancelling a מצוה only for a certain time, like 'no שבת in שביעית,' counts as partial cancellation. So the בית דין is liable.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the proof of step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A ruling of 'no שבת in שביעית' is partial cancellation, so the court is liable.

steps.title: When the court is exempt despite a mistaken ruling
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists cases where a בית דין's mistaken ruling does not make it liable for a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the בית דין ruled, and one judge knew they were wrong and told them 'You are mistaken,' the court is exempt. It is also exempt if the מופלא of the court was not there. It is also exempt if one judge was a גר, a ממזר, a נתין, or an old man who can no longer have children.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists cases where the court is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court brings a קרבן only for a full, proper ruling. That means a unanimous ruling, with the court's top expert present and every judge fit to judge. If any of these is missing, the ruling does not count as a ruling of the court.

keyTerms.meaning: the most expert member of the court
a child of a forbidden relationship
an old man who can no longer have children

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If the court issued a ruling,
and one of them knew that they erred,
and he said to them: 'You are mistaken,'

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מוּפְלָא שֶׁל בֵּית דִּין שָׁם,
phrases.english: or if the most distinguished member of the court was not there,
or if one of them was
a convert, or a mamzer, or a Gibeonite,
or an old man not able to have children,
this court is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין וְיָדַע אֶחָד מֵהֶן שֶׁטָּעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית דין is exempt from a קרבן if one judge objected, if the מופלא was absent, or if any judge was unfit.

steps.title: The source: the word 'עדה'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה learns its rule from a גזירה שוה. The word 'עדה' appears both here and in the case of the accidental killer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'עדה' is said here, and 'עדה' is said there. Just as in the 'עדה' said there, all the judges must be fit to rule, so too in the 'עדה' said here, the court is liable only if all the judges are fit to rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a source for why every judge must be fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word 'עדה' is used for the court here and for the court that judges a killer. That court must have only fit judges. So the court here also counts only if all its judges are fit.

keyTerms.meaning: here / there (the two places the word appears)

steps.whatToRemember: A court's ruling counts only if every judge is fit to rule. This is learned from the word 'עדה.'

phrases.english: As 'assembly' is stated here,
and 'assembly' is stated there,
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:24, the court that judges an accidental killer.

phrases.english: just as the 'assembly' stated there
all are fit to issue rulings,
so too the 'assembly' stated here,
not until all of them are fit to issue rulings.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כָּאן עֵדָה וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן עֵדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה's rule about unfit judges.
steps.raayaObject: That the court is liable only if all its judges are fit to rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on 'עדה' from ויקרא 4:13 and במדבר 35:24.

steps.title: What is the source for the missing distinguished member?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a בית דין is exempt if its most distinguished member was not there.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said the court is exempt if its most distinguished member was not there. Where do we learn that from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed the missing מופלא as a reason the court does not bring a קרבן. That rule is not obvious, so the גמרא wants to know where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The most distinguished, expert member of the court
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Or if there was not

phrases.aramaic: מוּפְלָא שֶׁל בֵּית דִּין שָׁם – מְנָלַן?
phrases.english: the most distinguished member of the court there, from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה's list of exemptions to ask the source for one item on it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for exempting the court when the מופלא was absent.

steps.title: They should have learned and did not
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת, backed by the school of רבי ישמעאל, compares the missing מופלא to a ruling on something the צדוקים agree to. In both cases the judges should have learned and did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said, and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught the same: Why is a court exempt when it rules on something even the צדוקים agree to? Because the judges should have learned it and they didn't. In the same way, if the most distinguished member was not there, they are also exempt, because they should have learned and did not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question. He uses the reason behind a known rule, a ruling on something the צדוקים agree to, and applies that same reason to the missing מופלא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some mistakes count as a real 'ruling of the court' and bring a קרבן. Other mistakes are simple failures to learn, and those do not count. Ruling without the court's top expert falls into this second group, just like getting an open Torah law wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: צדוקים, a group that accepted only the written Torah
A law so clear in the Torah that even the צדוקים agree to it
They should have learned and did not
The school of רבי ישמעאל taught

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives one shared reason for two different exemptions. A court's error brings a קרבן only if it is a real mistake in ruling, not plain neglect of learning.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said,
and so too the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
For what reason did they say

phrases.aramaic: הוֹרוּ בְּדָבָר שֶׁהַצַּדּוּקִין מוֹדִין בּוֹ פְּטוּרִין?
phrases.english: that if they ruled on a matter the Sadducees agree to, they are exempt?
phrases.notes: This is a law written openly in the Torah. Even people who reject the oral Torah accept it.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם לִלְמוֹד וְלֹא לָמְדוּ,
phrases.english: Because they should have learned, and they did not learn.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה מוּפְלָא שֶׁל בֵּית דִּין שָׁם
phrases.english: If the most distinguished member of the court was not there,
they are also exempt,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם לִלְמוֹד וְלֹא לָמְדוּ.
phrases.english: because they should have learned, and they did not learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The judges should have learned and did not. Like a ruling on something the צדוקים agree to, this is not a real ruling of the court, so they are exempt.

steps.title: Where do we learn that all judges must be fit to rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's גזירה שוה on 'עדה', which requires every judge to be fit to rule. It then asks where that requirement comes from in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'עדה' is said there and 'עדה' is said here, so all the judges must be fit to rule. And there, where do we learn that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's comparison again. It does this to ask a new question: where does the original case get the rule that every judge must be fit to rule? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה only moves a rule from one place to another. So the rule must already be known in the first place, and the גמרא wants its source.

keyTerms.meaning: Assembly, here meaning the court of judges

phrases.english: 'Assembly' is stated there
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה, the same comparison as in step 15.

phrases.english: and 'assembly' is stated here,
so they are not liable unless all of them are fit to issue rulings.
And there, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the גזירה שוה from step 15 and asks for the source of the rule in the original case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that all judges in the original case must be fit to rule.

steps.title: 'With you' means similar to you
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns it from the elders who would stand 'with you' (with משה). He reads 'with you' as 'like you'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The verse says, 'They shall stand there with you.' 'With you' means people similar to you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a source. The elders chosen to join משה had to be 'with you,' meaning like משה, fit to rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עמך' is read as a description of the judges' quality, not just where they stand. Like משה, they must be fit to give rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall stand there with you

phrases.english: As Rav Ḥisda said:
The verse says: 'And they shall stand there with you.'
'With you' means people similar to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'והתיצבו שם עמך': 'עמך' means judges similar to משה.

steps.title: Maybe 'with you' is about the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Maybe 'with you' means the elders should be like משה in being fit for the שכינה, not fit to rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead that 'with you' means fit for the שכינה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's proof. 'Like you' could mean something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that verse the elders were about to receive the spirit of נבואה. So 'similar to you' could easily mean worthy of the שכינה resting on them. If so, the verse says nothing about being fit to rule.

phrases.english: But say that 'with you' is about the Divine Presence!
phrases.notes: He means: like משה in being worthy of the שכינה resting on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's reading of 'עמך' as 'fit to rule'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In context, 'similar to you' could mean worthy of the שכינה, so the verse does not prove fitness to rule.

steps.title: A better source: 'and they shall bear it with you'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a different verse, 'ונשאו אתך'. It comes from the setting up of judges, so 'like you' there clearly means fit to judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The verse says, 'And they shall bear it with you.' 'With you' means people similar to you.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first verse was pushed aside, the גמרא gives a new source. This verse is about judges who share משה's load.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) shows the first source is dropped. This verse comes from יתרו's advice about appointing judges, so 'like you' can only mean fit to judge, and the שכינה reading does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: And they shall bear it with you

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that every judge must be fit to rule comes from 'ונשאו אתך'. Judges must be 'like משה' in their ability to judge.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
The verse says: 'And they shall bear it with you.'
'With you' means people similar to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 20 and replaces רב חסדא's source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'עמך' from the elders' verse proves the judges must be fit to rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אתך' from the verse about appointing judges proves it, since there it can only mean fit to judge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'ונשאו אתך' (שמות 18:22), said about appointing judges: 'אתך' means judges similar to משה, that is, fit to rule.

steps.title: New משנה: mistaken or intentional ruling and action
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets out three cases. The answer depends on whether the court ruled by mistake or on purpose, and whether the people acted by mistake or on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the court ruled by mistake and the whole community acted by mistake, the court brings a פר. If the court ruled on purpose and the people acted by mistake, each person brings a female lamb or female goat. If the court ruled by mistake and the people acted on purpose, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three combinations of the court's ruling and the people's action, and what each one brings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court brings the communal פר only when both sides acted by mistake. If the court knew its ruling was wrong, it is not a real error of the court, so each sinner brings a personal קרבן. If the people knew the ruling was wrong and followed it anyway, they sinned on purpose, and no קרבן applies.

keyTerms.meaning: A bull, the communal sin-offering for a court's mistake
A female lamb or female goat, an individual's sin-offering

steps.confusionAlert: In the second case the court is not the one bringing anything. Each person who sinned brings his own קרבן.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If the court ruled by mistake,
and the whole community acted by mistake,
they bring a bull.
If the court ruled on purpose and the people acted by mistake,
they bring a female lamb or a female goat.
If the court ruled by mistake and the people acted on purpose,
these are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין שׁוֹגְגִין, וְעָשׂוּ כָּל הַקָּהָל שׁוֹגְגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The communal פר comes only when both the court and the community acted by mistake. If the court ruled on purpose, each individual brings a כשבה or שעירה. If the community acted on purpose, they are exempt.

steps.title: An inference from the משנה's last case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the court ruled by mistake and the people sinned on purpose, they are exempt. It infers that a mistaken act that looks like an on-purpose one would be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if the court erred by mistake and the people did it on purpose, they are exempt. That implies that if a person acted by mistake, but in a way similar to doing it on purpose, the court is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and pulls out a hidden lesson. This sets up the next question about what such a case looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists only 'on purpose' as exempt. So the גמרא reasons that a mistaken act is still liable even if it looks a lot like an on-purpose act.

phrases.english: GEMARA
If they ruled by mistake and the people acted on purpose
these are exempt.
This implies: one who acted by mistake, similar to on purpose,
is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the last case of the משנה in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mistaken act that looks like an on-purpose one still makes the court liable.

steps.title: What would such a case look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a real example of a mistaken act that is similar to an on-purpose one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a concrete example of the inference it just made. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Mistaken but similar to on purpose' sounds like it contradicts itself. So the גמרא needs a real case to show how both can be true at once.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? how does it look?

phrases.english: And what are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an example of the inference in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete case of a mistaken act that is similar to an on-purpose one.

steps.title: The case: confusing forbidden fat for permitted fat
steps.stepSummary: The court ruled that חלב is permitted. A person then mixed up חלב with permitted fat (שומן) and ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court ruled that forbidden fat is permitted. This person mistook it for permitted fat and ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the example. The person would have eaten the חלב anyway because of the ruling, but he actually ate it by mixing it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He would have eaten it on purpose based on the court's ruling, so it is 'similar to on purpose.' But in fact he thought it was שומן, so he ate it by mistake. The inference says the court is liable in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: it got mixed up for him

phrases.english: Where the court ruled that forbidden fat is permitted,
and it got mixed up for him with permitted fat,
and he ate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person ate חלב after mistaking it for שומן, at a time when the court had ruled חלב permitted.

steps.title: Can this settle רמי בר חמא's question?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this inference answers רמי בר חמא's open question about exactly this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say: this settles the question that רמי בר חמא asked!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the inference from the משנה as proof for an earlier unanswered question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא asked whether this kind of mix-up counts as acting 'on the basis of the ruling.' The inference from the משנה seems to answer yes, since it says the court is liable.

phrases.english: Shall we say: resolve from here
that which רמי בר חמא asked!
phrases.notes: He asked about this exact mix-up case earlier in the מסכת, and it was left unanswered.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תִּפְשׁוֹט הָא דְּבָעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference of steps 23-25 to try to settle an earlier question.
steps.raayaObject: רמי בר חמא's question about someone who ate חלב after mixing it up with שומן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from 'שוגגין ועשו מזידין פטורין' in the משנה.

steps.title: The clause only matches the first clause
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא could answer that the משנה wrote this clause only to match the style of the first clause, so we cannot learn anything from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: since the תנא taught in the first part 'the court ruled on purpose and the people acted by mistake,' he taught in the last part 'the court ruled by mistake and the people acted on purpose.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns down the proof. The wording of the last case is just there to mirror the first case, so we should not draw an inference from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the exact wording 'on purpose' in the last clause. The rejection says that wording was chosen for style, to match the first clause. So רמי בר חמא's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: the teacher of the משנה taught

steps.whatToRemember: We cannot draw an inference from the משנה's last clause, because it was written to match the first clause. רמי בר חמא's question remains unanswered.

phrases.english: He could say to you:
Because he taught in the first part:
They ruled on purpose and the people acted by mistake,
he taught the last part:
They ruled by mistake and the people acted on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof built on the inference from the last clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording 'on purpose' in the last clause is just there to mirror the first clause. It is not chosen to teach a precise rule.

steps.title: New משנה: רבי מאיר says the court brings the קרבן
steps.stepSummary: If the court ruled wrongly and all or most of the people acted on it, a פר is brought. For עבודה זרה, a פר and a שעיר are brought, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the court ruled and all the congregation or most of them acted on its word, they bring a bull. For idol worship, they bring a bull and a goat. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says which קרבן is brought when the people follow a mistaken court ruling, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a regular sin the קרבן is one פר. When the mistake involves עבודה זרה, a שעיר is added. רבי מאיר holds that one set of קרבנות is brought for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: the whole congregation or most of it

phrases.english: MISHNA
If the court issued a ruling

phrases.aramaic: וְעָשׂוּ כׇּל הַקָּהָל אוֹ רוּבָּן עַל פִּיהֶן
phrases.english: and the whole congregation or most of them acted on their word,
they bring a bull.
And in a case of idol worship,
they bring a bull and a goat,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, one פר is brought for a mistaken ruling, and a פר and שעיר for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: each tribe brings its own קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that twelve tribes bring twelve bulls, and for עבודה זרה twelve bulls and twelve goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: twelve tribes bring twelve bulls. For idol worship they bring twelve bulls and twelve goats.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר. He says the קרבן is brought for each tribe, not one for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats each שבט as its own 'קהל.' So the number of קרבנות is multiplied by twelve: one פר per tribe, and for עבודה זרה also one שעיר per tribe.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: one פר (plus a שעיר for עבודה זרה) for everyone. רבי יהודה: twelve of each, one for every tribe.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:
Twelve tribes
bring twelve bulls.
And in a case of idol worship
they bring twelve bulls
and twelve goats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opinion that disagrees with רבי מאיר in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, each of the twelve tribes brings its own פר, and for עבודה זרה also its own שעיר.
